description: Registry of insurance traps, misunderstandings, claim risks, and advisor warnings.
principle: This registry captures where customers may misunderstand coverage and where claim disputes commonly arise.

entries.trigger: Actual room category or room rent exceeds policy eligibility.
entries.customer_misconception: Customer may think only extra room rent will be deducted.
entries.actual_meaning: Depending on policy wording, associated medical expenses may also be reduced proportionately.
entries.advisor_warning: Explain room eligibility and proportionate deduction clearly, especially for low sum insured plans.

entries.trigger: Policy has mandatory or conditional co-pay.
entries.customer_misconception: Customer may think co-pay applies to total bill or may not realize it applies on admissible claim amount.
entries.actual_meaning: Policyholder bears a percentage or amount of the admissible claim depending on policy terms.
entries.advisor_warning: Explain when co-pay applies: age-based, zone-based, treatment-based, hospital-based, or all claims.

entries.trigger: Customer has declared or undeclared pre-existing disease.
entries.customer_misconception: Customer may think all diseases are covered immediately after policy purchase.
entries.actual_meaning: Pre-existing diseases are covered only after the specified waiting period, subject to disclosure and policy conditions.
entries.advisor_warning: Ask medical history questions and compare PED waiting periods before recommendation.

entries.trigger: Claim is for a listed disease or treatment within disease-specific waiting period.
entries.customer_misconception: Customer may think only pre-existing diseases have waiting periods.
entries.actual_meaning: Certain diseases or treatments can have separate waiting periods even if they were not pre-existing.
entries.advisor_warning: Review disease-specific waiting period tables for customers with planned or likely treatments.

entries.trigger: Claim is for disease/procedure with a specific sub-limit.
entries.customer_misconception: Customer may assume full sum insured is available for every treatment.
entries.actual_meaning: Some diseases, procedures, or benefits may have separate caps within the overall sum insured.
entries.advisor_warning: Highlight sub-limits for common high-cost procedures and compare against customer needs.

entries.trap_name: Consumables and Non-medical Items Exclusion Trap
entries.trigger: Hospital bill includes non-medical or consumable items not covered by policy.
entries.customer_misconception: Customer may assume the entire hospital bill is payable by insurer.
entries.actual_meaning: Consumables and non-medical expenses may be deducted unless covered by add-on or policy benefit.
entries.advisor_warning: Check whether consumables cover or non-medical expenses cover is available.

entries.trigger: Customer expects restored sum insured to be available for same illness/member/claim.
entries.customer_misconception: Customer may believe restoration always refills coverage for any future or ongoing claim.
entries.actual_meaning: Restoration may be restricted by same illness, related illness, same insured person, first claim, or exhaustion conditions.
entries.advisor_warning: Identify restoration trigger and usage restrictions before highlighting as a selling point.
